page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-400s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring a dedicated AMD EPYC processor with 2 vCPUs, mapped from 1 physical core with 2 threads. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, the x86_64 CPU is supported by 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes 400 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and excludes any dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server achieves strong single-core performance, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2934.07 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2115.0, both placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core and parallelized workloads show significant limitations; the Geekbench multi-core score of 3785.0 and the Passmark CPU score of 5470.65 fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with large-block read and write speeds averaging 74.28 GB/sec and 53.91 GB/sec respectively.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing. The generous 400 GB NVMe SSD provides ample local storage, but the low vCPU count limits throughput in highly concurrent tasks. This is reflected in poor static web serving throughput of 2.26 GB/sec and weak database operation scores. Consequently, this server is best suited for memory-optimized, low-concurrency workloads such as small-scale caching, single-threaded text processing, lightweight background workers, or development environments requiring a larger memory footprint.
